primary.title: TrumpFile and Noel Casler Allege 1997 Miss Teen USA Rehearsal Conduct
primary.description_short: TrumpFile and Noel Casler separately allege rehearsal conduct at the 1997 Miss Teen USA pageant; the incident remains unverified and their accounts conflict on Ivanka Trump’s age.
primary.description_medium: TrumpFile.org dates its Miss Teen USA entry to August 20, 1997 and alleges that Donald Trump asked co-host Ivanka Trump for a lap dance during rehearsal. Noel Casler posted a similar allegation in 2020, but his post says Ivanka was 16 while TrumpFile says she was 15; a 2016 SFGATE report also described her as 16. These sources document attributed claims, not independent confirmation of the alleged conduct or its precise date.
primary.description_long: TrumpFile.org dates its Miss Teen USA timeline entry to August 20, 1997 and alleges that Donald Trump asked his daughter Ivanka, a co-host, for a lap dance during rehearsal. In a public post on January 21, 2020, former entertainment staffer Noel Casler made a similar allegation, writing that Trump called Ivanka over during a rehearsal and that she gave him a lap dance in view of the crew. These statements remain allegations; the retrieved materials do not independently establish that the conduct occurred. The sources also conflict on Ivanka’s age. TrumpFile says she was 15, while Casler’s post says 16 and a 2016 SFGATE report describes her as 16 at the pageant. The exact rehearsal date is not identified, and the pageant timeline’s date should not be treated as a verified date for the alleged incident. TrumpFile also groups this claim with accounts about contestants’ dressing rooms, but the supplied evidence does not establish that those accounts describe the same incident. Keep the allegations attributed and the age and chronology unresolved unless stronger contemporaneous or independent evidence becomes available.
primary.date_precision: TrumpFile timeline date; exact rehearsal date is not established.

source_fact_map.fact: A 2016 SFGATE report says Ivanka was 16 and co-hosted the pageant, conflicting with the age stated by TrumpFile. It does not report the alleged lap dance.
source_fact_map.quote: Ivanka Trump, the reality star’s daughter, was just 16 years old at the time and served as co-host of the event alongside actor J. Eddie Peck, according to footage of the pageant.
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: SFGATE, by Kelsey Bradshaw, published October 13, 2016: “The 1997 Miss Teen USA beauty pageant, where contestants said Donald Trump walked in on naked teenagers in the dressing room, was held on South Padre Island in Texas. The pageant, now almost 10 years ago, was the first under Trump’s tenor after he bought Miss USA, Miss Teen USA and Miss Universe in 1996. Ivanka Trump, the reality star’s daughter, was just 16 years old at the time and served as co-host of the event alongside actor J. Eddie Peck, according to footage of the pageant.”

frozen_original.title: Trump Ends DACA — 700,000 Dreamers Face Deportation
frozen_original.synopsis: On September 5, 2017, Attorney General Jeff Sessions announced the end of Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA), the Obama-era program protecting approximately 700,000 young immigrants who had grown up in the United States from deportation. Sessions falsely claimed DACA was unconstitutional, though it had withstood legal scrutiny for years. The termination gave Congress six months to act, but no legislative replacement was passed. Federal courts repeatedly blocked the full dismantling of DACA. The Supreme Court ruled in Department of Homeland Security v. Regents of the University of California (2020) that the rescission was 'arbitrary and capricious.' The decision left hundreds of thousands of young people who had known no other country in prolonged legal limbo.

frozen_original.title: Trump Threatens North Korea with 'Fire and Fury'
frozen_original.synopsis: On August 8, 2017, Trump warned North Korea that any further threats would be met with 'fire and fury like the world has never seen' — improvised language evoking nuclear annihilation that alarmed military officials, allies, and arms control experts. The statement was made off-the-cuff and had not been approved or coordinated with the National Security Council, State Department, or Defense Department. Secretary of State Rex Tillerson immediately tried to tamp down the rhetoric by assuring Americans they could 'sleep well at night.' Former diplomats warned the language could cause North Korea to miscalculate and take pre-emptive military action. The episode revealed Trump's willingness to freelance on nuclear threats without institutional review.

frozen_original.title: DHS creates anti-American list including academics, activists, journalists
frozen_original.synopsis: The Department of Homeland Security compiled an anti-American watchlist that included academics, activists, and journalists, using a vague and politically-motivated label to target critics of the administration. The list was reportedly maintained by a DHS unit with access to federal law enforcement databases, allowing listed individuals to face heightened scrutiny at border crossings, for security clearances, and in government contracting. Civil liberties groups obtained documents revealing the list included prominent journalists and Nobel Prize-winning scientists.

primary.title: Private Group Publishes Watchlist of Federal Health Workers
primary.description_short: The American Accountability Foundation, a private group, published a federal health-worker watchlist; the accessed report does not identify it as a DHS program.
primary.description_medium: The Guardian reported that the American Accountability Foundation (AAF), a private conservative watchdog group, published a healthcare-worker watchlist online on January 28, 2025. The list included names, photographs, and work histories of 57 mostly Black employees from federal health agencies. This repaired entry covers the documented private-group list, not the frozen claim that DHS created an “anti-American” list or used it for border, clearance, or contracting decisions.
primary.description_long: On January 28, 2025, the American Accountability Foundation (AAF), a private conservative watchdog group, published an online watchlist of federal health workers, according to The Guardian. The report said the list included names, photographs, and work histories of 57 mostly Black employees from several healthcare agencies; many had worked in health-equity roles. AAF president Thomas Jones said the group sought to target senior federal civil servants it viewed as promoting diversity, equity, and inclusion. The Guardian reported that one employee feared the list could harm careers or safety, but it did not establish that those feared consequences had occurred. This repaired entry replaces the frozen assertion that the Department of Homeland Security created an “anti-American” watchlist of academics, activists, journalists, and Nobel laureates. The accessed reporting identifies AAF as the publisher of a private list. It does not establish that DHS created the healthcare list, that AAF’s list gave its publishers access to law-enforcement databases, or that listed people faced heightened border checks, security-clearance decisions, or contracting consequences. Those government attribution and impact claims remain unsupported and are excluded.
